scope: Serial CPU diagnostic/algorithm reference; no distributed grants or hardware implementation.
domain: Every available boundary electrical node has exactly two SLR memberships. Constructor rejects catalogs with more memberships. Canonical IDs and original directed PIPs are unchanged.
die_sequence: Same deterministic multisource shortest simple die sequence used by the corridor planner. All existing tree seeds on its starting die are included. Optional reentry comparison separately searches a sequence starting outside the sink die.

edge_policy.internal_single_slr: Physical PIP must belong to the unique SLR of both electrical endpoints. That SLR must occur in the sequence.
edge_policy.internal_boundary: Enter on the earlier adjacent die and leave on the next die; using a boundary as an incidental same-die wire is prohibited.
edge_policy.root: Existing tree seeds may depart on the sequence starting die. Other existing tree nodes cannot be entered.
edge_policy.sink: End on the designated sink die, or enter a multi-SLR sink from the preceding die and terminate after its zero-hop transition; no outgoing PIP on the last die is required.
edge_policy.transition: Inside one electrical node, with no synthetic edge, cost, hop, or occupancy.

search: One existing guided sparse shortest-path search over all physical arcs admitted by the policy. Unchanged quotient potential remains a consistent relaxation; route cost is 1+history+present*other_net_count. Exact minimum cost/full-hop objective within this fixed-sequence family when search completes without resource cutoff. SparseSearch tie ordering is deterministic, not a claim of globally lexicographically minimal paths.
limitations: Not an oracle over other die sequences, die reentry, or global eventual shared trees.
A failed constrained discovery uses the unchanged full-graph fallback, with counters; a budget cutoff is not proof of unreachability.
Full physical WL/CPD and fresh DCP/STA signoff remain required.
reservation: Only after a complete discovered path, record the canonical union of selected portal IDs plus any new multi-SLR sink. Failure during discovery creates no reservation. Losing complete candidates and exceptions release their union. No strict capacity grant is implied.
journal: joint_searches is separate from local_searches and flat_searches. Failed joint discovery has failed_stage=UINT32_MAX-1 and every portal field=UINT32_MAX (no chosen corridor). Successful paths reconstruct the actual die transitions. Independent verifier checks PIPs, costs, release counts, authority and shadow replay.
shadow: Complete decision-read journal and stale serial replay are unchanged. Pure local/nonboundary costs still read centralized authority.
